title: Jealousy of God
definition: The jealousy of God is His holy zeal for His own glory and for the covenant faithfulness of His people.
summary: God's jealousy is His righteous refusal to share His glory with idols.
christFocus: Jesus calls His people to wholehearted devotion and frees them from false gods.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God's jealousy is not insecurity or sinful envy. It is His righteous zeal for what is good, true, and holy. God alone is worthy of worship, and idolatry destroys those who give themselves to it.

Because God loves His people, He refuses to treat spiritual adultery as harmless. His jealousy guards worship, covenant faithfulness, and the glory that belongs to Him alone.

Christ rescues idolaters and calls them into single-hearted devotion to God.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: People often treat idols as harmless comforts or personal preferences. The jealousy of God matters because it reveals the seriousness of divided worship.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Ask what competes with God's place in your heart. Turn from idols of approval, comfort, control, money, power, or pleasure, and worship the Lord with whole-hearted devotion.
